summary: Restoration targets 15 million trees by 2030, 5,000 ha of degraded forest and woodland by 2035—about 0.8% of current forest cover—and at least 100,000 ha of degraded rangeland, equivalent to 36.4% of current grassland. Conservation includes fire-management plans in 10 forest-adjacent communities, climate-resilient land-use plans in five chiefdoms by 2035, and at least three OECMs. Agriculture seeks climate-smart practices on 50,000 ha of cropland by 2035 (about 8.0% of current agriculture), manure management on 20% of commercial livestock farms, and irrigation efficiency of at least 70% by 2030. Mixed commitments rehabilitate 75,000 ha of communal grazing by 2035 (27.3% of current grassland), raise soil organic carbon by an average of 5% across 30,000 ha of agricultural and grazing land by 2035, and conserve 174,000 ha while restoring 150,000 ha by 2035—about 10.0% and 8.6% of total land, respectively.
